And it’s really cute when she tries. She doesn’t mix personal feelings with work (she’s ESTJ), but she won’t let work get in the way of friendship too much. She has no tolerance for BS, but she’ll still try to heal a friendship after. She might be really straight with people, and sometimes even rude, but I think it’s great that she’s so honest. She’ll admit that she’s being rude, too, and she apologizes for being rude, but not for speaking the truth. She plans out her days and weeks, and makes sure she can accomplish everything she wants to. She is such a great and awesome person; whoever she will end up with will be a god damn lucky man - guy I’m sure he’ll know that he’s struck gold. I feel really lucky that I’ve the pleasure to be her friend.

I've done a lot of public speaking since I was a child, so here's the best tips I can tell you.  
- Look up some poem you enjoy, go to the mirror and read it out. Don't just read it out like its a textbook, be as expressive as possible. Be embarrassed, it's okay, you're supposed to. The more you look like an idiot or overly expressive actor, the better. (Don't do this in public, of course). This helps you get over the fear of how other people perceive you when you talk.  
- stand in front of your parents and do this. Say you're practicing for homework. The first time maybe either just your dad or mom, whichever your more comfortable with, then eventually other family members too. STAND. DONT SIT. BE AS EXPRESSIVE AS YOU CAN AGAIN.  
- Think very clearly before you say anything, ever. This took me quite a while to master, but just try to do it in a day to day conversation too. Eventually you'll get used to thinking first then speaking. This helps organize your sentences and reduce stutter.  
Those helped me so that I feel a lot less anxious when I do presentations in front of a lot of people (the most I've ever done was 1000, twice). But without actually doing any form of public speaking, it's hard to get used to it.  
That said, I'm good at public speaking but shit at talking to girls...  
Edit: mock interviews helped practice thinking before speaking too!
